subject: URGENT: us-west-2 latency & 5xx spike — request for geo-fallback to us-east-1
messages:
From: Anna Sorensen <anna@quantumbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: spiky 5xx and 3x latency in us-west-2 (urgent)

Hi Marissa / Marcus,

We just observed a sharp degradation in the us-west-2 region starting ~09:05 PDT — our customer-facing API is seeing a sustained 5xx rate (~12%) and tail latency has increased ~3x (p95 ~1.8s -> 5.6s) for the Redwood model route we're calling. Throughput has fallen ~40% relative to baseline. Screenshot attached (usw2_latency_screenshot.png).

This is impacting live traffic for our product search and we've already received two high-priority support tickets. Can Redwood trigger cross-region fallback to us-east-1 or otherwise route traffic away from the impacted AZ? We need an immediate mitigation and an estimate for time-to-stabilize.

Also: can you confirm whether this will cause any model-version/quantization mismatch on the fallback path? We prefer identical model variant if possible.

- Anna
CEO, QuantumBridge

Attachment: usw2_latency_screenshot.png (image/png)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sorensen <anna@quantumbridge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spiky 5xx and 3x latency in us-west-2 (urgent)

Thanks for the heads up, Anna — we see the PagerDuty alert as well and I’m escalating immediately. Marcus/ops, tagging Vanessa and Rishi for ops/SRE coverage.

Vanessa: please confirm whether we can open a geo-fallback to us-east-1 now and what the expected RTO is. If we need an exec sign-off for a canary threshold change or temporary capacity bump, Marcus is on copy.

Marcus: I’ve included the customer screenshot and the tickets (linked in PD). Quick ask — please confirm we can route QuantumBridge traffic to the identical model variant in us-east-1; they explicitly asked to avoid a quantized variant fallback if possible.

I’ll stay on the thread and coordinate customer comms.

- Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer_screenshot.png (image/png)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spiky 5xx and 3x latency in us-west-2 (urgent)

Quick ops update: we’ve started a traffic steering policy to shift new sessions away from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) but the current canary threshold is defined in the routing policy at 30% and requires Ops lead approval to override to 50% for faster evacuation.

Immediate notes:
- We can perform a targeted routing override for QuantumBridge only (route tag = qb-account) to move 100% of traffic to us-east-1 within ~90s after the override, subject to capacity.
- Capacity note: us-east-1 has spare Dedicated capacity but it will incur overage/burst billing for the first 3 hours.
- Model variants: we have the same model family in us-east-1 on identical GC/quantization profile for their account; I’m verifying the exact model hash with Rishi.

Requesting a quick sign-off to: (1) override canary to 50% now, (2) initiate full account-only redirect if metrics improve on canary. Marcus, please advise on cost/exec guidance; I’ll hold on the override until we have your go.

PD: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-982341
Runbook: https://redwood-internal.company/runbooks/geo-fallback

-Vanessa
Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: geo-fallback-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spiky 5xx and 3x latency in us-west-2 (urgent)

On 2028-06-10 09:35 -07:00 Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> Quick ops update: we’ve started a traffic steering policy to shift new sessions away from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) but the current canary threshold is defined in the routing policy at 30% and requires Ops lead approval to override to 50% for faster evacuation.

Thanks — we’re seeing the same in metrics. Short technical note:
- Root symptoms: increased model serving queue times in AZ us-west-2a caused by a local GPU host OOM/eviction cascade; this is manifesting as queue time and occasional 5xx from the runtime.
- We have identical model binary and quantization profile (sha256: d4f8b3...) deployed in us-east-1, so model mismatch risk is low.
- Current action: warmed new KV caches in us-east-1 for the affected model, primed embeddings and prefix caches for active keys. Expect steady-state latency to drop to baseline within ~45-75s after 50% canary shift; throughput should return to ~90% of baseline within 3-5 minutes as caches fill.
- Risk: if we do an immediate 100% redirect without canary, we risk transient 502s from cold KV cache; recommended path is 50% override -> monitor 1 minute -> 100% redirect.

Metrics snapshot: https://metrics.redwood.company/snapshots/20280610/0918 (attached as metrics_snapshot-0918.csv)

I support the targeted account-only redirect and approve the 50% override now if leadership signs off on the cost/overage.

- Rishi
SRE Manager

Attachment: metrics_snapshot-0918.csv (text/csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sorensen <anna@quantumbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spiky 5xx and 3x latency in us-west-2 (urgent) — executive sign-off

Anna — thanks for raising this and for the screenshot. Short update and exec sign-off below.

Executive summary:
- What happened: an OOM/eviction cascade impacted a subset of hosts in AZ us-west-2a causing elevated queue times and 5xx for your account’s model route.
- Immediate mitigation: we will approve a targeted account-only routing override to shift QuantumBridge traffic to us-east-1. Ops will set canary to 50% immediately, monitor for 60s, then move to 100% if the canary stabilizes (per Rishi’s guidance).
- Model safety: SRE confirms identical model hash and quantization profile exist in us-east-1; we’ll avoid fallback to a quantized mismatch.
- Customer impact: expected p95 latency back to baseline within ~1 minute of successful 50% canary; throughput ~90% baseline in 3-5 minutes.
- Billing: this will trigger a temporary burst/overage in Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 for the next ~3 hours; we will credit QuantumBridge for the incremental overage for this incident.

Next steps (owners):
- Vanessa: execute 50% override now and monitor (Ops).
- Rishi: validate cache warmup and confirm 100% redirect when safe (SRE).
- Marissa: update Anna and the two open support tickets with status and expected timelines (AE).
- Marcus (me): follow up with an incident summary + credit note within 48 hours and coordinate a post-incident RCA call.

Anna — will you confirm that routing to us-east-1 is acceptable? We’ll proceed on your confirmation or proceed after 5 minutes if we don’t hear back (to limit customer impact).

Thanks — we’ll keep you updated on each step.

- Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
